title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: Consolidated company-wide policies and process references covering access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates.
body:
Purpose and scope

Purpose: Provide a single, authoritative reference for company-wide operational policies and end-to-end processes that affect multiple teams and business functions.
Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, vendors with network access, and any systems housing Redwood corporate data. This doc covers policy principles, mandatory procedures, escalation paths, and links to templates and request forms.

Roles & responsibilities

People Ops (owner): policy maintenance, travel & expense governance, onboarding/offboarding coordination.
Security (co-owner): access controls, vendor security assessments, data classification, incident response tie-ins.
Finance (owner for procurement & expenses): PO approvals, corporate card management, auditing and spend reporting.
IT/Cloud Infrastructure: implement access controls, maintain service accounts, enforce encryption and backups.
Team Leads / Managers: approve role-based access, change requests, travel and expense requests for direct reports.
Change Advisory Board (CAB): cross-functional review for medium/large changes; schedule and approval authority defined below.

Access & permissions

Principles
- Least privilege: users receive the minimum access required for their job function.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): standard roles (engineer, infra-admin, SRE, analytics, product, sales) are the default assignment vectors.
- Segregation of duties: no single individual should hold unrestricted prod admin, billing, and security-review privileges.

Standard onboarding/offboarding flow
1. Manager raises an Access Request (template) during onboarding.
2. People Ops verifies headcount and employment status.
3. Security and IT provision accounts: corporate SSO, email, Slack, Jira, Confluence, CI/CD, cloud console roles.
4. Manager verifies access within 5 business days.
5. Offboarding: People Ops initiates account disablement on termination date; access removed within 4 hours of HR system action for involuntary terminations.

Access request and approval process
- Low-risk (non-prod dashboards, read-only analytics): auto-approve by manager via Access Request form; target SLA: 24 hours.
- Medium-risk (write access to non-prod infra, deploy rights in staging): requires manager + infra owner approval; SLA: 48 hours.
- High-risk (prod access, admin roles, billing): requires manager + security + service owner approval; CAB notification if change affects multiple services; SLA: 5 business days.
- Emergency access (break-glass): time-limited sessions via privileged access manager (PAM); require post-hoc justification and 72-hour review by Security.

Service accounts and keys
- Service accounts must be documented in the Service Account Registry (link in related pages).
- Long-lived secrets are prohibited; use short-lived credentials and vault (KMS/Secrets Manager) integration.

Audit and reviews
- Quarterly access review led by Security. Managers must certify current access for direct reports.
- Any discrepancies must be remediated within 10 business days and reported to the CTO and Head of Security.

Change management

Change categorization
- Standard changes: low-risk routine changes with pre-defined runbooks (e.g., small config changes). Manager approval required.
- Normal changes: planned infrastructure or app changes that require technical review and a change ticket.
- Major changes: architectural changes, production-impacting releases, database migrations, security-sensitive updates — require CAB approval and pre-change runbook + rollback plan.

Change process (step-by-step)
1. Create a Change Request ticket in Jira using the change-request template.
2. Include risk assessment, rollback plan, test plan, and scheduled window.
3. If Normal or Major, notify CAB at least 72 hours before proposed window.
4. CAB reviews: impact analysis, scheduling, and dependencies. Approval recorded in Jira.
5. Change owner executes the runbook; on completion, update ticket with artifacts and post-change validation results.
6. Post-change review: for Major changes, run a 3-day and 30-day follow-up to verify metrics and incidents.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Standard maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for non-critical infra work.
- Blackout windows: major product launches, scheduled customer events; CAB will publish blackout windows quarterly.

Emergency change handling
- Emergency changes must be declared in the incident channel and by an authorized on-call engineer.
- Post-facto documentation required within 24 hours and CAB review within 72 hours.

Data management

Data classification
- PUBLIC: information intended for public consumption (marketing, public docs). No special controls.
- INTERNAL: company-internal but not sensitive (internal process docs). Store in internal docs; no external sharing without approval.
- RESTRICTED: PII, customer metadata, internal financials. Access limited to approved roles; encryption at rest & in transit required.
- CONFIDENTIAL: regulated data, customer-protected data, legal/HR sensitive records. Strict access, full audit logging, and retention controls.

Handling rules
- All RESTRICTED and CONFIDENTIAL data must be stored in approved systems only (Redwood-approved cloud storage, secure DBs). No personal devices or consumer cloud storage.
- Encryption: At rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. KMS-managed keys; key rotation policy: every 12 months or after suspected compromise.
- Masking & anonymization: Use tokenization or hashing for datasets used in analytics or test environments.

Retention and deletion
- Retention schedules are defined per data type (finance = 7 years, HR = 7 years after termination, analytics aggregated = 12 months by default).
- Data deletion requests (user or customer) must follow the Data Deletion Playbook and be completed within 30 days unless legal hold applies.

Backups and recovery
- Critical systems: daily backups with 30-day retention and an annual restore test.
- Backup encryption and immutable storage for production DB backups.

Data access review and breach handling
- Quarterly data access audits, with anomalies escalated to Security within 48 hours.
- Suspected data breach process: follow incident response runbook; notify Legal, Security, and People Ops; customers notified per contractual obligations and jurisdictional regulations.

Procurement & expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals
- Low-value purchases (< $2,000): Team lead approval.
- Medium ($2,000–$25,000): Team lead + Finance approval.
- High (> $25,000): Procurement lead + Finance + Legal review; may require executive sponsor.

Purchase order (PO) process
1. Requestor completes PO request form and selects budget code.
2. Finance validates budget and issues PO.
3. Vendor delivers goods/services; Finance reconciles invoice with PO before payment.

Corporate cards and expenses
- Corporate cards issued on manager nomination; card limits set by Finance.
- Expense reimbursement: submit receipts via expense portal within 30 days; approvals required from manager.
- Per diem and travel allowances: follow the Travel Policy section below.

Cost controls and tagging
- Cloud resources must include cost center tags; infra will enforce tagging with automated policies.
- Procurement team runs monthly vendor spend reports and flags unusual spend to Finance and the Requesting Manager.

Auditing and recordkeeping
- Finance retains procurement records per financial retention policy (7 years).
- Random procurement audits run semi-annually; non-compliance may result in revocation of procurement privileges.

Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Business owner submits Vendor Request form with scope and expected spend.
- Security performs a vendor risk assessment (questionnaire + SIG profile) for vendors with access to RESTRICTED or CONFIDENTIAL data.
- Legal completes contract review and includes standard security clauses (data processing addendum, breach notification timelines, rights to audit if data access allowed).
- Finance validates payment terms and PO requirements.
- Onboarding complete only after contract signed, PO issued (if required), and security controls verified.

Vendor risk tiers
- Tier 1 (High risk): Vendors with access to customer or regulated data — require SOC2/ISO27001 or equivalent plus annual review.
- Tier 2 (Medium): Vendors with internal system access but no sensitive data — require security questionnaire and quarterly checks.
- Tier 3 (Low): Standard SaaS with public controls; minimal onboarding checklist.

Third-party access controls
- Limit vendor access to least privilege and time-bounded credentials. Use vendor-specific accounts and monitoring.
- All vendor access to prod must be approved by the service owner and Security, with PAM where applicable.

Offboarding vendors
- Terminate credentials, remove network ingress rules, recover company assets, and verify data deletion per contract within 7 business days of contract termination.

Travel policy

Booking and approvals
- All travel must be booked via the corporate travel portal or Travel Ops team for exceptions.
- For domestic travel, manager approval is required. For international travel, People Ops and manager approval required.

Allowances and per diem
- Standard per diem for domestic travel: $75/day; international per diem varies by region (use travel portal defaults).
- Business class allowed for flights > 8 hours with VP-level approval.

Expense submission and reimbursement
- Submit itemized receipts within 30 days via expense portal. Missing receipts require manager exception.
- Credit card charges should be reconciled monthly. Fraud or disputed charges must be reported within 7 days to Finance.

Travel safety & security
- Employees traveling internationally must register with Travel Ops and check-in on arrival for higher-risk countries.
- Emergency contacts and insurance information available through People Ops.

Templates and forms (internal)
- Access Request Form: /templates/access-request
- Change Request Template: /templates/change-request
- Vendor Risk Assessment: /templates/vendor-risk-assessment
- PO Request Form: /templates/po-request
- Travel & Expense Template: /templates/travel-expense
- Data Deletion Playbook & Template: /templates/data-deletion

Exceptions and policy changes
- Exceptions: must be submitted to People Ops or Security with justification, compensating controls, and a sunset date. Executive sponsor required for exceptions > 90 days.
- Policy update cadence: People Ops + Security review this document annually or after major organizational changes. Ad-hoc updates published with change history.

Enforcement and consequences
- Non-compliance may result in revocation of privileges, retraining, disciplinary action, or termination depending on severity.
- Finance and People Ops will audit expense and procurement compliance; Security will audit access and data handling.

Contacts and escalation
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Security (co-owner): security@redwood.com
- Finance & Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- IT/Cloud Infrastructure: cloud-ops@redwood.com
